post_topic: HITL gates must be first-class architecture, not afterthoughts in agentic systems
image_description:
Single standalone diagram. One concept only. No panels, no grids, no collages. Full bleed 1080x1080px white background.

Title at top in bold navy: 'HITL Gate Placement: Afterthought vs. Architecture'.

Diagram is a left-to-right horizontal flow split into two rows, clearly labeled.

Top row label (left side, amber #F5A623 text): 'WRONG — Gate as Apology'.
Flow nodes left to right: [Agent Step 1] → [Agent Step 2] → [Agent Step 3 — Decision + External Write] → [Agent Step 4] → [Agent Step 5] → [Agent Step 6 — Output] → [Human Review ✗] (this final node is small, dashed border, grey, visually de-emphasized). A small amber callout arrow points to the grey Human Review node with label: 'Irreversible action already happened on Step 3'.

Bottom row label (left side, blue #5a96ff text): 'RIGHT — Gate as Load-Bearing Checkpoint'.
Flow nodes left to right: [Agent Step 1] → [Agent Step 2] → [HUMAN CHECKPOINT ✓] (this node is large, solid amber #F5A623 fill, bold border, navy text, visually dominant — largest box in the diagram) → conditional split: top branch arrow labeled 'Approved' leads to [Agent Step 3 — External Write]; bottom branch arrow labeled 'Rejected' leads back to [Agent Step 1] with a curved return arrow. Then [Agent Step 3] → [Agent Step 4 — Output].

Small annotation below bottom row in navy italic: 'Gate sits at the trust boundary — before the irreversible action.'

No other elements. Arrows are clean and directional with arrowheads.

Navy #0A0F1E primary elements, blue #5a96ff highlights, amber #F5A623 callouts and important labels. Clean sans-serif font. Real cloud provider logos where relevant. Small text 'Kelvin Davis' bottom right corner. Professional LinkedIn infographic style similar to ByteByteGo. White background. No dark backgrounds.
